equation_request.abstract: We consider the quantum time complexity of the all pairs shortest paths (APSP) problem and some of its variants. The trivial classical algorithm for APSP and most all pairs path problems runs in $O(n^{3})$ time, while the trivial algorithm in the quantum setting runs in $\tilde{O}(n^{2.5})$ time, using Grover search. A major open problem in classical algorithms is to obtain a truly subcubic time algorithm for APSP, i.e. an algorithm running in $O(n^{3-\varepsilon})$ time for constant $\varepsilon>0$. To approach this problem, many truly subcubic time classical algorithms have been devised for APSP and its variants for structured inputs. Some examples of such problems are APSP in geometrically weighted graphs, graphs with small integer edge weights or a small number of weights incident to each vertex, and the all pairs earliest arrivals problem. In this paper we revisit these problems in the quantum setting and obtain the first nontrivial (i.e. $O(n^{2.5-\varepsilon})$ time) quantum algorithms for the problems.

specification.problem: Quantum time complexity of all pairs shortest paths (APSP) and variants. Only the trivial Grover-search baseline and the complexity targets are stated in the abstract. The actual nontrivial quantum algorithms are not described.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Scoped to the trivial Grover-based quantum baseline for one primitive: finding a minimizing intermediate vertex w for a single pair (u,v) in a tiny n-vertex weighted graph, via Grover/quantum minimum finding. The paper's nontrivial O(n^{2.5-eps}) algorithms for geometric weights, small integer weights, few weights per vertex, and earliest arrivals are out of scope.

equations.description: Doing quantum minimum finding for each of n^2 pairs gives the n^{2.5} (up to polylog) trivial bound.

registers.name: k
registers.role: index of candidate intermediate vertex for a fixed pair (u,v)

steps.description: Prepare the uniform superposition over candidate intermediates k for a fixed pair (u,v).
Compute d_1(u,k)+w(k,v) into the workspace via a data oracle (assumed).
Apply Grover/Durr-Hoyer minimum finding with O(sqrt(n)) iterations.
Repeat for all n^2 pairs to obtain the trivial total cost.

specification.measurement: Measure the k register after minimum finding to obtain the argmin (assumed).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Store the minimum value for each pair (u,v) and combine into the distance matrix.
assumptions: No scope was given, so the trivial Grover baseline for one pair was chosen as the smallest useful construction.
Quantum access to the weight matrix is assumed to be a standard query oracle.
